evidence.author_statement: a major component in the extracts was (E,Z)-2,13-octadecadien-1-ol acetate along with traces of (Z,Z)- and (Z,E)-isomers
evidence.notes: About 100 prepupal larvae collected from Cucurbita pepo, overwintered outdoors in soil, moved to 16L, 24 C in March; about 15 females emerged. Females held about 48 h, calling 13:00-14:00; ovipositors excised and soaked individually in 40 ul heptane for 1 h. Only 4 extracts had enough titre; these were combined (Table 1 percentages). Others showed negligible E,Z-2,13-18:OAc. Identity by retention on Supelcowax and DB-1; GC-MS of the silica acetate fraction confirmed 1, 6, 7, 8 and 10 and showed a trace octadecadienyl acetate at peak 2,12; the alcohol fraction, acetylated, gave spectra identical to the acetates of 4, 5 and 9. Peak 2,12 is assigned to Z,Z-3,13-18:OAc 'by inference only' from the field tests. The abstract calls all minor compounds probable. Hydrocarbons C23, C25, C27 also present.
unresolved: peak 2,12 is one peak, Z,E-2,13-18:OAc or Z,Z-3,13-18:OAc; Table 1 lists both at 0.1 percent. Recorded once, as Z,Z-3,13-18:OAc, the authors' assignment 'by inference only' from the field tests; the abstract instead lists traces of the (Z,Z)- and (Z,E)-2,13 isomers
peak 11,13 is one peak (0.2 percent), Z,E- or E,Z-3,13-18:OAc, which the authors leave unassigned; not recorded as either
where the larvae were collected

evidence.notes: Muddy cocoons from a vineyard in Tottori Prefecture in winter; three females and two males emerged after about two months. Abdominal ends of one-day-old calling virgin females, each in hexane for 5 min. 1.0 FE on GC-MS (DB-23). Z3,Z13-18:OH and Z3,Z13-18:OAc: retention equal to the synthetics in GC-EAD and spectra 'quite similar' to them. The three minor compounds: 'the chromatographic behavior and spectral data of these compounds suggested the following chemical structures', with no further chemistry because the extract was limited, so tentative. Ratio about 100:5:1:1:2 (Z3,Z13-OH : Z3,Z13-OAc : E3,Z13-OH : E3,Z13-OAc : Z13-OH) from the TIC. The (3E,13E)- and (3Z,13E)-isomers of the acetate and alcohol were undetectable in the mass chromatograms (Fig. 1C, D).

titre per female
detection limit for the negatives

evidence.author_statement: Two GC-EAD-active components were found in a crude extract of M. japona female pheromone gland, and identified as (2E,13Z)-2,13-octadecadien-1-ol (E2,Z13-18:OH) and (2E,13Z)-2,13-octadecadienal
evidence.notes: About 40 overwintering larvae from Maihara City, November 2003, vernalised 2 months at 8 C, then 25 C, 15L:9D. Abdominal tips of 1- or 2-day-old virgin females excised when calling, each in 250 ul hexane for 5 min. Ten GC-MS injections (1 FE each) of different extracts: E2,Z13-18:OH 0.3 +- 1.2 and E2,Z13-18:Ald 4.2 +- 5.4 ng per female (mean +- SD), 'roughly 1:10' with 'considerable variation'. Alcohol: Florisil 10 percent ether fraction, mass spectrum like synthetic E2,Z13-18:OH (M+ vs M-18 intensities separate 2,13 from 3,13 dienols), retention equal to it and unlike the other three 2,13 isomers on DB-23. Aldehyde: 5 percent ether fraction, spectrum like synthetic E2,Z13-18:Ald, and NaBH4 reduction of the fraction gave E2,Z13-18:OH. The authors note identification was by comparison with known compounds, not direct chemistry. E2,Z13-18:OAc not detected (Fig. 1b mass chromatograms).
unresolved: detection limit for E2,Z13-18:OAc

evidence.author_statement: In these pheromone extracts, no acetate components were detected.
evidence.notes: About 40 overwintering larvae collected at Toyota City, Aichi, December 2003, vernalised for a month, reared at 23 C, 13L:11D. Calling induced by direct sunlight; abdominal tips of 1-2-day-old virgin females extracted singly in 250 ul hexane for 5 min. Titres from eight GC-MS injections of 1 female equivalent each (whether each was one female is not stated; extracts were combined two female equivalents at a time for Florisil): 12.3 +- 10.8 and 1.4 +- 1.3 ng per female, a ratio of about 9:1 despite large individual variation. The acetates are recorded as negatives because the authors had synthetic 3,13 acetates as references and state none were detected; the detection limit is not given. The authors call it the first sesiid known to secrete these two alcohols as pheromone components without any acetate.

evidence.author_statement: the percentages of E3,Z13-18:OH; Z3,Z13-18:OH; E2,Z13-18:OH; Z13-18:OH and 18:OH from the sex pheromone gland extracts of 3 females were found to be 64.0 : 32.4 : 1.4 : 0.9 :1.3
evidence.notes: Pupae from Populus spp. at Kandagash (Rynkum sandy-hill steppe), 29 May - 1 June 2001, adults emerged in individual cages. Abdominal tips of calling females (afternoon) pushed out, excised and washed twice in 20 ul hexane for 2 min; three glands extracted in all, concentrated to about 10 ul. One DB-5 column; chromatograms screened by diagnostic ions (m/z 61, 248, 250, 252), then identity by mass spectrum and retention against synthetic standards. Geometry therefore rests on retention on one non-polar column (Atlas reading). abundance_class 'major' for E3,Z13-18:OH is the Atlas reading of 64 percent and of the title's 'minor' components for the rest. The Chinese identification (Zhang et al. 1986) found only E3,Z13-18:OH.

whether acetates and aldehydes were absent (the screen used m/z 61 but no negative is stated)

evidence.author_statement: both 1a and 1d gave strong EAG responses, while the other two appeared rather weak
evidence.notes: Synthetic isomers at 1 and 0.1 ug: EZ 1.5 and 0.5 mV, ZZ 1.5 and 0.5 mV, EE and ZE 0 and 0. EE and ZE are recorded inactive on the printed numbers and Fig. 3; the text's wording is in unresolved.

evidence.author_statement: The natural pheromone was shown to be identical to 1a with Rt of 17.05 min
evidence.notes: Ovipositor areas of 1- to 2-day-old unmated females (50 FE), clipped and extracted with CH2Cl2; insects reared on artificial diet (origin not stated). GC-MS on SE-54: spectrum and retention identical to synthetic E3,Z13-18:OH. Mass fragmentography (m/z 266, 248) on FFAP separated the four synthetic isomers (ZZ 18.12, ZE 17.40, EZ 17.05, EE 16.42 min); the natural peak matched EZ, and co-injection enhanced only that peak. The text states no absence. The negatives here are read from Fig. 2B (Atlas reading): the extract's m/z 266 (M+) trace is flat at the retention times of the EE, ZE and ZZ standards in Fig. 2A, with only the EZ peak. The m/z 248 trace cannot exclude ZE or ZZ, because an unassigned, off-scale m/z 248 peak covers that window; Karalius et al. 2001 suggest minor compounds may have been below detection. Beijing area is where the field tests ran; where the insects came from is not said.
unresolved: whether any other compound, including the other 3,13 isomers, was absent (no negative is stated)
amount per female
origin of the reared insects
detection limit of the m/z 266 negatives
a large unassigned m/z 248 peak just after the EZ peak (about 17.2-18 min) and a smaller one near 18.8 min in Fig. 2B

One ratio is given for both populations. Same gland chemistry as spa.obs.sesia_apiformis.francke_2004.spme_individual, sampled differently.

evidence.author_statement: SPME collections from effluvia of calling females showed the ratio of the major compounds to be 13 ± 3%:87 ± 3% (N = 5)
evidence.notes: SPME fibre held a few mm from the gland for 2-4 h while calling; only compounds released exclusively during calling were analysed. E2,Z13-18:OH, present in gland extracts, was not detected in the effluvium.
unresolved: whether ± is SD or SE (recorded as SD)
which population the five females came from

comparator.description: each compound alone (200 micrograms alcohol; 300 micrograms aldehyde); neither caught males

context.locality: Roskilde, Hojby and Sidinge, Zealand, Denmark

evidence.author_statement: When synthetic compounds were tested alone or as mixtures in the ratios identified in extracts of abdominal tips of females, only blends were attractive
evidence.notes: July 23 - August 1, 1996; 5 replicates. Zero-catch lures were excluded from Duncan's test, so no test is stated against single compounds.

comparator.description: each compound alone (200 micrograms alcohol; 300 micrograms aldehyde); neither caught males

evidence.author_statement: only blends were attractive
evidence.notes: July 29 - August 15, 1996; 5 replicates. In 1997 (Table 2) alcohol:aldehyde from 30:300 to 300:300 micrograms were all attractive and not different; 300:90 caught fewer and 300:30 none, so the effective range covers both the extract (2:3) and SPME (about 1:7) ratios.

comparator.description: binary alcohol 200 + aldehyde 300 micrograms, without E2,Z13-18:OH

evidence.author_statement: when 200 µg of 2E,13Z-18:OH were added to 500 µg of the binary mixture, the attractiveness of the lure was significantly reduced
evidence.notes: Table and text disagree. In Table 3 the 200-microgram lure (2.5, letter b) shares a letter with the binary blend (4.7, ab), so it is not significantly different from it; it differs from the 2-microgram lure (6.1, a). Recorded as not significant against the stated comparator, with the authors' wording kept. June 16 - July 15, 1997.

evidence.author_statement: An electroantennographically active substance has been isolated

responses.notes: response to 1-min GC fractions of a female extract; the active fraction was later assigned to Z3,Z13-18:OH; the pure synthetic compound was not tested by EAG

evidence.author_statement: has been identified as a sex pheromone
evidence.notes: Only the EAG-active alcohol fraction was pursued, so the aldehyde found in 2004 (Francke et al.) was not examined: not_tested, not absent. The authors' label 'sex pheromone' is kept as their statement; later work found this alcohol unattractive alone.
unresolved: collection locality: cocoons dug from poplar trunks; one author affiliation is the Donetsk Botanical Garden, but the site is not stated

comparator.description: each compound alone (100 micrograms); neither caught males

evidence.author_statement: strongly attracted male Synanthedon andrenaeformis
evidence.notes: A field attractant with the E3 isomer dominant, the reverse of S. tipuliformis's optimum. 3 replicates; 1985: 11.7. No gland analysis.

evidence.author_statement: No adult males were caught in traps baited with 9:1 or control traps.
evidence.notes: Experiment 1, Gongju, 28 April - 13 June 2017 (spring, Atlas label from the dates), green bucket traps, 4 blocks, one-way ANOVA and Tukey HSD (F4,15 = 38.567, P < 0.001). The authors give the optimum as about 4.3:5.7: that is this 4:6 lure corrected for purity, and no 4.3:5.7 lure was tested. Lures synthesised by the authors: 1 mg per sleeve-stopper septum with 1 mg BHT, changed monthly; traps 3 m up on roadside cherry trees, at least 15 m apart, re-randomised every two weeks. Purity is GC-MS peak area; the authors do not say what the impurities are and state that the lures held no isomeric compounds. Atlas reading of Fig. 4: the impurities are minor peaks 0.07-0.37 min after each main peak (13.763 and 13.903 min for E3; 13.745, 13.903 and 14.037 min for Z3), on a column where E3 and Z3 eluted 0.035 min apart in separate runs, so geometric isomers among them are not excluded. Means read from bar charts. Letters a vs c.

evidence.author_statement: One compound obtained from each species retained all the activity of the original extract
evidence.notes: Ovipositors of 800 1- to 3-day-old unmated females ground three times with pentane; silicic-acid LC (pentane-ether 95:5 fraction active), then sequential packed-column GC on SE-30, OV-101 and Carbowax 20M, guided by a field bioassay. The active compound was over 99.5 percent pure on SP-2300, Dexsil and DEGS. Structure from CI-MS, IR (trans band at 970/cm in S. pictipes; the text says the '960' band was absent in S. exitiosa), hydrogenation to octadecyl acetate, microozonolysis (valeraldehyde and 1,10-decanedial; the middle product decomposed, and its spectrum, consistent with 3-oxopropyl acetate, came only from the synthetic) and comparison with all four synthetic 3,13 isomers, of which DEGS completely resolved only the (E,E)-isomer. No abundance class: nothing else in the extract was characterised.

evidence.notes: Late-instar larvae dug from apple trunks at Suwon (37.2 N, 127.1 E), May-June 2008, reared on artificial diet at 23 C, 16L:8D; sexes separated at eclosion (virgin is the Atlas reading). Females call during the photophase; glands of 1- to 2-day-old females were taken 4 h into photophase, extruded and excised, each extracted 10 min in 10 ul hexane with 10 ng 13:OAc. Identity from MS library match, then retention indices and spectra against authentic standards on DB-Wax and DB-23 (Table 1 lists all four 3,13 and 2,13 isomers of the acetates and alcohols). DMDS derivatisation did not locate the double bonds. Ratio of peaks 1-9 0.2:1.5:0.4:3:2:87:100:1:1.5; E2,Z13-18:OAc 'estimated as 21.5 ng per female' (N = 15). Also C21, C23, C25 and C27 alkanes.

evidence.author_statement: The mixing ratios of Comps. I–III approximately converged at 36 : 60 : 4.
evidence.notes: Last-instar larvae from the Meijo University farm, Kasugai, reared at 25 C, 15L:9D. Abdominal ends of 1-2-day-old calling virgin females, 250 ul hexane for 5 min. Geometry rests on retention on one polar column (DB-23); the mass spectra do not separate the isomers (Atlas note). Titres from the GC-MS analysis repeated 'three times' with 4 female equivalents each after a first 4 FE run, so three or four runs (+- 2.2, 3.2, 0.2 ng; dispersion type not stated). E3:Z3 = 37.6:62.4 (Atlas note: Yang et al. 2011 cite it as 38:62). Negatives: no E3,Z13- or Z3,Z13-18:OH or E2,Z13-18:Al peaks at the retention times of their standards (Fig. 2B), and no E3,E13- or Z3,E13-18:OAc (Fig. 2A). Z2,Z13-18:OAc is not recorded as a negative: its standard elutes beside the Z3,Z13-18:OAc peak on DB-23, so retention alone cannot exclude it (Atlas reading; the same applies to the Z2,E13 and E2,E13 acetates, which have no Atlas record); no detection limit given. The abstract swaps the I/II labels (see the reference notes).
unresolved: whether the +- values are SD or SE

evidence.author_statement: Catches by all treatments in group 1 were significantly greater than all in group 2.
evidence.notes: Experiment 1, 21 June - 5 July 2007 (counted 28 June and 5 July), randomised complete blocks, 10 replicates, 8 delta traps 5 m apart in linear blocks 20-21 m apart; two-way randomised block ANOVA F7,63 = 4.47, P < 0.001, Tukey (alpha 0.05). Delta traps 21 cm long, 10 x 10 x 10 cm cross-section, painted inside and out with a gloss white base coat (Krylon Fusion) then a high-gloss Ecologic acrylic (Cloverdale Paints); clear traps left unpainted; lure pinned at the upper centre; traps about 1.5 m up in the canopy; sticky bases. Lure: grey halobutyl rubber septum (West Co.) loaded with 1 mg Z3,Z13-18:OAc (Pherobank, >95% isomeric purity) in 200 µL hexane; the micro sign was checked in the PDF font stream: '1 mg' is set in the text font, '200 µL' uses the symbol font. Means read from the bar chart (Fig. 1B), Atlas reading; letters b vs a. The abstract sorts clear, white, green and yellow into group 1 and purple, blue, red and black into group 2, every group-1 trap catching significantly more than every group-2 trap. Atlas reading of Fig. 1A (words only): white about 80% flat above ~410 nm; yellow rises at ~500-520 nm to ~70%; green peaks near 530 nm (~60%); blue peaks near 460 nm; purple peaks near 420 and 660 nm; red rises above ~570 nm; black near zero throughout; clear was measured as acetate over the white standard (~85%, neutral). The authors group yellow, green and white as similarly high at 500-550 nm.

evidence.author_statement: the (Z,Z)-isomer, in concentrations as low as 1 percent, significantly reduced the response of S. pictipes males to their pheromone
evidence.notes: Significance as the authors state it for 1 percent and above. Fig. 2: average number of males responding, five replicates, read from the bar chart; bars below 1 are about the drawn baseline thickness and may be zero. The figure does not label which axis row is the (E,Z)-isomer; the Atlas reads the top row as (E,Z) because S. pictipes peaks at 100. Total 120 ng per test is the Atlas reading of the legend, which gives an equivalence (about 30 FE of S. pictipes, about 1 FE of S. exitiosa), not a stated load; the text's units differ, see the reference notes. Assay of note 8, as the Atlas reads it: material in pentane in a glass petri dish on the ground, males responding counted over 35 min; the paper names Byron, Georgia only for the earlier bioassays, so locality is left null. The text says the mixtures were compared with the 99.5+ percent pure isomers, not that they were made from them; no purity is recorded. No test statistic or per-ratio comparison is printed.

evidence.author_statement: One compound obtained from each species retained all the activity of the original extract
evidence.notes: Ovipositors of 25,000 1- to 3-day-old unmated females ground three times with methylene chloride; silicic-acid LC (pentane-ether 95:5 fraction active), then sequential packed-column GC on SE-30, OV-101 and Carbowax 20M, guided by a field bioassay. The active compound was over 99.5 percent pure on SP-2300, Dexsil and DEGS. Structure from CI-MS, IR (trans band at 970/cm in S. pictipes; the text says the '960' band was absent in S. exitiosa), hydrogenation to octadecyl acetate, microozonolysis (valeraldehyde and 1,10-decanedial; the middle product decomposed, and its spectrum, consistent with 3-oxopropyl acetate, came only from the synthetic) and comparison with all four synthetic 3,13 isomers, of which DEGS completely resolved only the (E,E)-isomer. No abundance class: nothing else in the extract was characterised.

evidence.notes: Six groups of 3-10 virgin females (1-13 days old) aerated 3-7 days on Super Q, eluted with methylene chloride; Fig. 1B is 48 h of effluvia from seven females aged 3-13 days. The three EAD-active FID peaks matched the retention times of Z,Z-3,13-, E,Z-2,13- and Z,E-3,13-ODDA on DB-WAXETR and DB-5; the first two were identified by co-injection in the gland extract, and their 'confirmed' here rests on the effluvium peaks being the same compounds (retention on two columns; Atlas reading, no GC-MS of the effluvia is reported); the third only by retention, so tentative as the authors say. n_individuals is the Fig. 1B run (seven females); the identification drew on all six groups.
unresolved: amounts and ratio in the effluvia (the 88:6:6 'estimated' ternary ratio is not tied to a stated analysis)
whether the effluvia were analysed by GC-MS

sample.material_as_reported: volatiles from groups of 3-10 virgin females trapped on Super Q and eluted with methylene chloride

evidence.author_statement: GC-EAD analyses of the four synthetic geometric isomers of 3,13-ODDA revealed that all elicited significant EAD responses
evidence.notes: Fig. 1: two EAD responses in a gland extract of two females, three in effluvia of seven; the third (Z,E-3,13-ODDA) 'sometimes elicited EAD responses'. Table 1, synthetic 10 ng, N = 3, mean +- SD mV: E,E-3,13 0.13 +- 0.03 ab, Z,E-3,13 0.24 +- 0.04 a, E,Z-3,13 0.30 +- 0.09 a, Z,Z-3,13 0.30 +- 0.10 a, E,Z-2,13 0.20 +- 0.13 ab; Z,E-, Z,Z- and E,E-2,13 0.03-0.05 b. Fig. 1C: synthetic Z,Z-3,13 and E,Z-2,13 'also elicited strong antennal responses'. 'Active' for the synthetics follows the text (all four 3,13 isomers 'significant'; E,Z-2,13 'strong' in Fig. 1C); by the Table 1 letters alone, the 'ab' responses (E,E-3,13, E,Z-2,13) are not separable from the 'b' group.
unresolved: number of antennae for the extracts
whether the 0.03-0.05 mV readings to the other three 2,13 isomers count as responses (not recorded)

evidence.author_statement: only two peaks were deleted, at the retention times of Z,Z-3,13-ODDA and E,Z-2,13-ODDA, and with a ratio of 94:6
evidence.notes: Larvae dug from apple burrknots in Jefferson and Berkeley Counties (WV) and Frederick County (VA), October-November 2002 and 2003, reared on diet at 25 C, 16L:8D; adults emerged at Beltsville. Glands of 2- to 13-day-old virgin females (previously aerated), everted ovipositors soaked at least 2 h in methylene chloride-methanol 3:1 and re-extracted; combined extract of 20 females on GC-MS (DB-WAXETR). Z,Z-3,13-ODDA confirmed by GC-EAD retention on DB-WAXETR and DB-5 and co-injection; E,Z-2,13-ODDA by co-injection on GC-MS. 'Deleted' in the source is read as 'detected'. Z,E-3,13-ODDA, seen in effluvia, was not detected in gland extracts by SIM.
unresolved: detection limit of the SIM negative

sample.material_as_reported: ovipositors excised into about 100 ul methylene chloride-methanol (3:1), soaked at least 2 h, re-extracted; 20 glands combined

evidence.author_statement: Rubber septa loaded with 1 mg doses of binary and ternary blends attracted more males than traps baited with one virgin female (Figure 6).
evidence.notes: Fig. 6, August 16 - September 13 2004, 763 males, N = 4, F = 25.72; letters: virgin female b, binary a, ternary a. Caged 2- to 4-day-old virgin female, one per cage. Commercial apple orchards; traps about 1.2 m up, randomized within three to five rows separated by buffer rows, at least about 20 m apart, rotated weekly; 1 mg per septum, compounds as the parts printed under each bar. Z,Z-3,13-ODDA (Bedoukian, about 90 percent) purified on silver-nitrate silica to under 0.3 percent E,Z-3,13-ODDA; the other isomers (PheroBank) checked above 97 percent on DB-WAXETR. Means read from the bar chart.

evidence.author_statement: The extract included only Z3,Z13-18:OAc, but no alcohols or aldehydes were detected.
evidence.notes: About 20 larvae from a persimmon orchard, January 2002, reared at 25 C, 15L:9D; nine females emerged and all were extracted, 1-2 days old, calling 12-15 h after lights on. Titre 'about 2 ng/female' from five 1-female-equivalent GC-MS runs (N = 5). Geometry from retention on DB-23 (KI 2639) against all four 3,13 isomers; the authors note the EI spectra of the isomers are quite similar, and the diagnostic ions suggested the 3,13 positions. Negatives: no peaks at the retention times of the other three 3,13 acetates, E2,Z13-18:OAc, E3,Z13- and Z3,Z13-18:OH, or E2,Z13-18:Al (Fig. 2). Z2,Z13- and E2,E13-18:OAc are not recorded as negatives: their standards elute at or beside the Z3,Z13-18:OAc peak in Fig. 2a, so retention alone cannot exclude them (Atlas reading). Atlas note: Korean S. tenuis glands showed the reverse, Z3,Z13-18:OH present and Z3,Z13-18:OAc absent below about 100 pg (spa.obs.synanthedon_tenuis.yang_2012.gland).

evidence.notes: Larvae from root collars of peach and nectarine, Kefar Tabor, March-June 2010, reared on a peach-cortex diet at 24 C in darkness. One-day-old calling females; samples of 1-3 glands in 20 ul hexane for 15 min. Ratio 83:17 from 15 samples; amounts 14.0 +- 6.2 and 2.9 +- 1.3 ng per gland from 25 females (dispersion type not stated). The authors call the ratio about 4:1 and used 4:1 in the field. The geometry rests on retention on DB-23: RTX-5 does not separate the 3,13 isomers (Table 1) and the mass spectra do not distinguish them (Atlas note). Negatives: no other octadecadienyl acetates (standards of all four 3,13 isomers and all four 2,13 acetates were run; the Z2,E13 and E2,E13 acetates have no Atlas compound record) and no corresponding alcohols, for which no standards are listed; no detection limit is given.

evidence.author_statement: (E,Z)-2,13-Octadecadien-1-ol acetate was identified from ovipositor extracts of the grape root borer
evidence.notes: Field-collected female pupae; adults emerged in the laboratory and ovipositors were extracted with heptane (method of Klun et al. 1980); seven females in all. One major peak: GC-MS M+ 308 and M-60 at 248 (octadecadienyl acetate); microozonolysis gave undecanedial (nine carbons between the double bonds) and no identifiable short aldehyde. Candidates Z,Z-3,14, Z,Z-4,15, Z,Z-5,16 (all four isomers), Z-6,17 and Z,Z-2,13 were excluded by retention; synthetic E,Z-2,13-18:OAc matched on SP2340, SP1000 and DB-1 with no difference in mass spectrum, and only one of the four isomers from thiol equilibration of Z,Z-2,13 co-eluted with it. A minor component eluting after it on non-polar columns had the spectrum of an octadecenyl acetate (position not determined).
